subject: Status update and coordination: HorizonAI service impact (SEV-1)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@horizonai.com>, HorizonAI Ops <ops@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 03:12:00 +0000
Subject: Service degradation observed — immediate coordination

Sophie / HorizonAI ops team,

We are seeing an elevated error rate and token-generation timeouts affecting a subset of requests routed through our eu-west region and some cross-region traffic. Initial telemetry shows increased latency in the KV-cache layer followed by partial request timeouts for longer sequences. Impact began at ~03:05 UTC.

Immediate actions we have kicked off:
- Spawned a dedicated bridge (INC-2026-091) and attached the infra and runtime on-call.
- Throttled large-batch traffic and temporarily disabled speculative execution for affected model family to reduce load on the cache layer.
- Gathering mitigation logs and a timeline (I will share the timeline shortly).

Sophie — we will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have a full mitigation. If you can, please share whether HorizonAI has any critical jobs running now that we should prioritize or pause.

Apologies for the disruption. My goal: reduce customer-facing errors within the next 2 hours and provide a clear post-incident timeline.

— Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sev1-incident-timeline.pdf (draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 03:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Service degradation observed — immediate coordination

On Tue, 1 Sep 2026 at 03:12, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sophie / HorizonAI ops team,
> 
> We are seeing an elevated error rate...

I’ve got infra and runtime working the cache eviction policy and a hotfix branch for the kernel path. Tentative plan: roll the hotfix to one pod pool as a canary in 20m, observe for 15m, then expand.

I’ll also collect the KV miss-rate graphs and attach the mitigation commands log after the canary.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-commands.log (in-progress)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@horizonai.com>, HorizonAI Ops <ops@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 04:05:00 +0000
Subject: [Update] Customer-facing summary & executive note — HorizonAI impact

Sophie, HorizonAI leadership,

Follow-up update and what you can expect from us now: we’ve declared this a SEV-1 given the user-facing errors and throughput degradation. High-level summary:
- Scope: ~12% of generation requests received a 500/timeout between 03:05–03:55 UTC (peak).
- Root-cause (initial): stressed KV-cache eviction path that surfaced under long sequence workloads for the v2 model family.
- Immediate mitigations performed:
  * Canary deployed hotfix to a shard of the pool (03:35 UTC), observed ~70% reduction in timeouts on canary traffic.
  * Disabled speculative execution across the affected pool (03:20 UTC) to stabilize latency.
  * Increased autoscaling headroom and temporarily rebalanced traffic away from eu-west KVs (03:40 UTC).

Current status (04:05 UTC): majority of user traffic is stable; error rate has dropped from peak but intermittent timeouts remain for long-sequence flows. Our SREs are continuing the safe rollback/expand of the canary.

Next updates:
- 04:35 UTC — progress on canary expansion and observed metrics.
- 05:30 UTC — mitigation verification and plan for re-enabling speculative execution (if stable).
- Postmortem package (timeline, root cause analysis, and actions) by EOD local time; preliminary timeline attached.

Customer asks / prioritization: please confirm whether you have any queued bulk inference jobs or scheduled experiments in the next 4 hours that we should de-prioritize to speed primary traffic recovery.

We will remain on this until fully remediated and will follow with an executive summary.

Best,
— Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sev1-incident-timeline.pdf (updated), customer-bridge-brief.txt

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@horizonai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: HorizonAI Ops <ops@horizonai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 04:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Update] Customer-facing summary & executive note — HorizonAI impact

Rafael — thanks for the clear update. We have two scheduled nightly batches that start at 05:00 UTC; please deprioritize those if it will help recovery. Our SRE will stand by on the bridge and can provide payload samples if useful.

Also: can you confirm whether there will be any data retention or data-loss risk for requests that timed out? Our compliance team will ask.

— Sophie Lang
Head of Platform, HorizonAI

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@horizonai.com>, HorizonAI Ops <ops@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:45:00 +0000
Subject: Final customer update for now — mitigation, data safety, and next steps

Sophie — quick wrap for your execs and compliance:

1) Current state - All canaries expanded to full pool; error rates are back within SLA for the v2 model family and long-sequence traffic is stable. We’re keeping elevated monitoring for the next 24 hours.

2) Data safety - No customer input data was dropped from durable stores. Timeouts occurred during runtime processing; requests that timed out did not persist to long-term storage and can be retried by your job runner without risk of silent data loss. We will include a clear statement in the postmortem.

3) What we’ll deliver by EOD - Full incident timeline (attached), root-cause analysis, remediation steps, and a remediation ticket list (with owners and ETA).

4) Immediate mitigations we will keep in place for 48h - conservative cache eviction thresholds, temporary speculative-execution guardrails for long sequences, and expanded autoscaling headroom for eu-west.

If HorizonAI wants a short exec call to summarize the incident and confirm SLAs and credits, I can set aside 30 minutes this afternoon.

Thanks for the fast coordination — Ben and Laura did the heavy lifting on the mitigation.

— Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sev1-incident-timeline.pdf, mitigation-commands.log, customer-bridge-brief.txt
